```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
options(width = 750)
has_diamond <- nzchar(Sys.which("diamond"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  comment = "#>",
  collapse = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  tidy = FALSE,
  eval = has_diamond)
```

The dN/dS ratio quantifies the mode and strength of selection acting on a pair of orthologous genes.
This selection pressure can be quantified by comparing synonymous substitution rates (dS) that are assumed to be neutral
with nonsynonymous substitution rates (dN), which are exposed to selection as they 
change the amino acid composition of a protein ([Mugal et al., 2013](https://academic.oup.com/mbe/article/31/1/212/1049986)).

The `orthologr` package provides a function named `dNdS()` to perform dNdS estimation on pairs of orthologous genes.
The `dNdS()` function takes the CDS files of two organisms of interest (`query_file` and `subject_file`) 
and computes the dNdS estimation values for orthologous gene pairs between these organisms.

The default method is Comeron's (1995), which is built into the package; `"Li"` (Li 1993) is computed with
`seqinr::kaks()`. Neither needs an external program.

__Note:__ the following dNdS estimation methods are based on KaKs_Calculator 2:

* "NG": Nei, M. and Gojobori, T. (1986)

* "LWL": Li, W.H., et al. (1985)

* "LPB": Li, W.H. (1993) and Pamilo, P. and Bianchi, N.O. (1993)

* "MLWL" (Modified LWL): Tzeng, Y.H., et al. (2004)

* "YN": Yang, Z. and Nielsen, R. (2000)

* "MYN" (Modified YN): Zhang, Z., et al. (2006)

* "GMYN": Wang, D.P., et al. Biology Direct. (2009)

* "GY": Goldman, N. and Yang, Z. (1994)

* "MS": (Model Selection): based on a set of candidate models, Posada, D. (2003) 
* "MA" (Model Averaging): based on a set of candidate models, Posada, D. (2003)

* "ALL": All models together 

It is assumed that when you choose one of these dNdS estimation methods you have
[KaKs_Calculator 2](https://sourceforge.net/projects/kakscalculator2/) installed on your machine and it can be executed from the
default execution `PATH`.

The following pipeline resembles an example dNdS estimation procedure:

 1) Orthology Inference: e.g. DIAMOND2 reciprocal best hit (RBH) — default; or BLAST reciprocal best hit
 
 2) Pairwise amino acid alignment of each gene pair: Needleman-Wunsch in R (`aa_aln_tool = "NW"`, the default), or an external
    multiple alignment program (`clustalw`, `clustalo`, `mafft`, `muscle`, `t_coffee`) with `aa_aln_type = "multiple"`
 
 3) Codon Alignment: e.g. pal2nal program
 
 4) dNdS estimation: Comeron (1995) by default; e.g. [Yang, Z. and Nielsen, R. (2000)](https://academic.oup.com/mbe/article/17/1/32/975527) (YN) with KaKs_Calculator


__Note:__ it is assumed that when using `dNdS()` all corresponding programs you
want to use are already installed on your machine and are executable via either
the default execution PATH or you specifically define the location of the executable program
via the `aa_aln_path` or `aligner_path` argument that can be passed to `dNdS()`. By default `dNdS()` uses DIAMOND2 (`aligner = "diamond"`); you can switch to BLAST by setting `aligner = "blast"`. See the [Sequence Alignments vignette](https://drostlab.github.io/orthologr/articles/sequence_alignments.html)
for details.

The following example shall illustrate a dNdS estimation process.


```{r,eval=has_diamond}
library(orthologr)
# get a dNdS table using:
# 1) DIAMOND2 reciprocal best hit for orthology inference (default; aligner = "diamond", ortho_detection = "RBH")
# 2) Needleman-Wunsch for pairwise amino acid alignments
# 3) pal2nal for codon alignments
# 4) Comeron for dNdS estimation
# 5) single core processing 'comp_cores = 1'
dNdS(query_file      = system.file('seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
     subject_file    = system.file('seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
     aligner         = "diamond",
     ortho_detection = "RBH", 
     aa_aln_type     = "pairwise",
     aa_aln_tool     = "NW", 
     codon_aln_tool  = "pal2nal", 
     dnds_est.method = "Comeron", 
     comp_cores      = 1)
```
Some outputs include `NA` values. To filter for `NA` values or a specific `dnds.threshold`,
you can use the `filter_dNdS()` function. The `filter_dNdS()` function takes the output data.table 
returned by `dNdS()` and filters the output by the following criteria:

1) all dN values having an NA value are omitted

2) all dS values having an NA value are omitted

3) all dNdS values >= the specified `dnds.threshold` are omitted


```{r,eval=has_diamond}
library(orthologr)
# get dNdS estimated for orthologous genes between A. thaliana and A. lyrata
Ath_Aly_dnds <- dNdS(query_file      = system.file('seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
     subject_file    = system.file('seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
     aligner         = "diamond",
     ortho_detection = "RBH", 
     aa_aln_type     = "pairwise",
     aa_aln_tool     = "NW", 
     codon_aln_tool  = "pal2nal", 
     dnds_est.method = "Comeron", 
     comp_cores      = 1)
# filter for:
# 1) all dN values having an NA value are omitted
# 2) all dS values having an NA value are omitted
# 3) all dNdS values >= 2 are omitted
filter_dNdS(Ath_Aly_dnds, dnds.threshold = 2)
```

The `dNdS()` function can be used choosing the following options:

* `aligner` : `"diamond"` (default; DIAMOND2) or `"blast"` (BLASTP)
* `ortho_detection` : `RBH` (reciprocal best hit), `BH` (best hit) — works with both DIAMOND2 and BLAST depending on `aligner`
* `aa_aln_type` : `pairwise` (default) or `multiple`
* `aa_aln_tool` : `NW` (default; with `aa_aln_type = "pairwise"`), or with `aa_aln_type = "multiple"`: `clustalw`, `clustalo`, `mafft`, `muscle` (3.8 or 5), `t_coffee`
* `codon_aln_tool` : `pal2nal`
* `dnds_est.method` : `Comeron` (default), `Li`, and with KaKs_Calculator `NG`, `LWL`, `LPB`, `MLWL`, `YN`, `MYN`, `GY`, `GMYN`, `MS`, `MA`, `ALL`

Please see `?dNdS` for details.

In case your DIAMOND2 program or multiple alignment program cannot be executed from the default execution `PATH`
you can specify the `aa_aln_path` or `aligner_path` arguments.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(orthologr)
# using the `aa_aln_path` or `aligner_path` arguments
dNdS( query_file      = system.file('seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
      subject_file    = system.file('seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
      aligner         = "diamond",
      ortho_detection = "RBH",
      aligner_path    = "here/path/to/diamond",
      aa_aln_type     = "multiple", 
      aa_aln_tool     = "clustalw", 
      aa_aln_path     = "here/path/to/clustalw",
      codon_aln_tool  = "pal2nal", 
      dnds_est.method = "Comeron", 
      comp_cores      = 1, 
      clean_folders   = TRUE)
```


## Good practice

**One transcript per gene.** `dNdS()` treats every sequence of a file as a gene. Files with all transcripts
(the `cds/all` files of Ensembl, files from `biomartr::getCDS()`) give several rows per gene with different
partners, and the splice variants compete as best hits: on human chromosome 21 such a file holds 2,048
sequences for 220 genes. `dNdS()` warns when it sees this; keep the longest isoform first with
`retrieve_longest_isoforms()` (it needs the annotation file) and run `dNdS()` on its output.

**Sequences that are left out.** Coding sequences with characters other than A, C, G, T are left out before the
search (they cannot be translated), also when it is a single leading `N` - 2.5 to 4.7 % of the Ensembl
transcripts of human and mouse chromosomes, almost none in RefSeq sets. Sequences whose length is not a multiple
of 3 are trimmed (`delete_corrupt_cds = FALSE`) or left out (`TRUE`). The summary at the end of the run gives the
number and `attr(result, "dropped_sequences")` lists them.

**Sensitivity of the search.** The default `sensitivity_mode = "fast"` is tuned for closely related species
(DIAMOND: hits of more than 90 % identity). For distant species it misses orthologs and saves almost no time:

| reciprocal best hits (DIAMOND, 2 cores) | `"fast"` | `"default"` | `"sensitive"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| *A. thaliana* / *A. lyrata*, 1,000-gene example | 983 | 985 | 985 |
| *S. cerevisiae* / *C. glabrata* | 4,164 (7 s) | 4,384 (8 s) | 4,502 (24 s) |

The pairs found only with `"default"` have a median identity of 37 % and a median length of 298 amino acids.
Use `sensitivity_mode = "default"` or `"sensitive"` when the proteins of the two species are less than about
70 % identical.

**Best hits.** `best_hit_rule = "bitscore"` (default) chooses the hit with the highest bit score;
`"evalue"` is the rule of 0.4.3, under which a paralog with a longer alignment could win when several hits have
an e-value of 0 (see the article "Upgrading from 0.4.3").

**Saturation and distant species.** Read the summary at the end of the run and the column `status`. A pair
with status `"saturated"` has changed at so many sites that dS (rarely dN) cannot be estimated; its `dNdS` is
`NA`. When a large part of the pairs is saturated, or the median dS is above 1.5, the two species are too
distant for pairwise dN/dS: *S. cerevisiae* against *C. glabrata* gives 4,164 pairs of which 3,012 (72 %) have
no dS, and a median dS of 1.9 for the others. dS values above about 2 carry little information even when a
number is returned. Compare more closely related species, or use dN alone.

**Filtering.** `filter_dNdS()` removes pairs without dN or dS, pairs with dS = 0 (`dS_zero = "keep"` keeps them
with `dNdS = NA`) and pairs above `dnds.threshold` (default 2), and says how many rows it left out for each
reason. Filter on `status == "ok"` and on dS explicitly when the analysis needs a stricter rule.

**Choice of method.** `dNdS()` runs PAL2NAL (Perl) and the estimation for one gene pair at
a time: about 50 ms per pair and core, i.e. about 17 minutes per 20,000 pairs on one core; use `comp_cores`.
Comeron's method (default) and Li's method need no further program; `"YN"`, `"NG"`, `"MYN"` etc. need
KaKs_Calculator.

**Keep the record.** `attr(result, "orthologr_run")` holds the versions, arguments, options and checksums of
the run; `write_dNdS(result, "file.tsv")` writes the table together with it. Report the version of orthologr and
any option you changed.

## Advanced options

Additional arguments can be passed to `dNdS()`. This allows you to use more advanced 
options of several interface programs.

To pass additional parameters to the interface programs, you can use the
`aligner_params` (DIAMOND2 or BLAST) and `aa_aln_params` (multiple alignment program) arguments. The `aa_aln_params`
argument assumes that when you chose e.g. `aa_aln_tool = "mafft"` you will pass the corresponding
parameters in MAFFT notation. It is handed to `multi_aln()` as `params` and __replaces__ the default
parameters of the program, so the alignment must still be written in CLUSTAL (or FASTA) format, e.g.
`--clustalout` for MAFFT. `aa_aln_params` is only used with `aa_aln_type = "multiple"` (until version 0.4.3 it was
accepted but not passed on to the alignment program).

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(orthologr)
# get dNdS estimated for orthologous genes between A. thaliana and A. lyrata
# using additional parameters:

# get a dNdS table using:
# 1) DIAMOND2 reciprocal best hit for orthology inference (RBH), with extra DIAMOND2 params
# 2) multiple amino acid alignments using MAFFT
# 3) pal2nal for codon alignments
# 4) Comeron (1995) for dNdS estimation
# 5) single core processing 'comp_cores = 1'
Ath_Aly_dnds <- dNdS( query_file      = system.file('seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
                      subject_file    = system.file('seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta', package = 'orthologr'),
                      aligner         = "diamond",
                      ortho_detection = "RBH",
                      aligner_params  = "--matrix BLOSUM80",
                      aa_aln_type     = "multiple",
                      aa_aln_tool     = "mafft",
                      aa_aln_params   = "--quiet --anysymbol --maxiterate 1 --clustalout",
                      dnds_est.method = "Comeron",
                      comp_cores      = 1, 
                      clean_folders   = TRUE, 
                      quiet           = TRUE )

# filter for:
# 1) all dN values having an NA value are omitted
# 2) all dS values having an NA value are omitted
# 3) all dNdS values >= 0.1 are omitted
filter_dNdS(Ath_Aly_dnds, dnds.threshold = 0.1)
```

```
     query_id      subject_id       dN     dS    dNdS
1 AT1G01050.1 909874|PACid:16 0.000000 0.1750 0.00000
2 AT1G01090.1 470171|PACid:16 0.009843 0.2150 0.04579
3 AT1G01120.1 918858|PACid:16 0.003072 0.1326 0.02317
4 AT1G01140.3 470161|PACid:16 0.005672 0.1312 0.04324
5 AT1G01170.2 311317|PACid:16 0.008750 0.2827 0.03095
6 AT1G01220.1 470155|PACid:16 0.015210 0.1533 0.09919

```
Here `aligner_params` and `aa_aln_params` take a character string specifying the parameters
that shall be passed to DIAMOND2 (or BLAST when `aligner = "blast"`) and MAFFT, respectively.
The notation of these parameters must follow the command line call of the stand alone versions
of DIAMOND2 and MAFFT: e.g. `aligner_params = "--matrix BLOSUM80"`
and `aa_aln_params = "--quiet --anysymbol --maxiterate 1 --clustalout"`.
